data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the test's failure is a necessary condition for the subject's later passage; under shown-to-fail-first installation, the 3-of-26 result is an artifact of the test's own failure being installed as a precondition, so the test describes the installation's history rather than constraining the mutation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the test's initial failure were removed and the 3 survivors still survived, the history hypothesis would be weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a different installation order produced a different survivor count, the artifact hypothesis would be supported.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the test's failure were shown to be causally unrelated to the mutation's later passage, the constraint hypothesis would be restored.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The shown-to-fail-first ritual makes the test's initial failure a part of the subject's history, so the test's later passage is a description of that history rather than a constraint on the mutation. The 3 survivors are mutations that were never subjected to a test whose failure was not already installed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
